expectation: Membrane rings at cell-cell junctions of epithelial cells: common, forming continuous honeycomb or chicken-wire outlines along glands and crypts and lining surfaces. Stroma and immune cells negative. May be weaker on invasive or poorly cohesive tumour cells.
observed: A: crypt and gland outlines light up across both sections. B, C: crisp honeycomb membrane rings on columnar epithelium around a lumen, stroma dim. D: membrane outlines around nuclei. E1 same; E2 panCK is hazy and blobby, so E tells little. Bright blobs are debris.
why: Crisp membrane honeycomb confined to the gland and crypt epithelium, with negative stroma, is the expected E-cadherin pattern; the bright blobs are artefacts and do not affect this.
